disclosures.name: TestAllocationsFromBytes/Atoi
disclosures.reason: Want-zero AllocsPerRun assert: the test's string(bytes.Number) argument is proven non-escaping by Go's compiler and stays on the stack; the managed model materializes an @string per run. Read at Atoi (src/core/strconv/atoi.cs:255-267), the counted objects are that argument, the function-local `"Atoi"u8` constant materialized per call, and `range []byte(s)` copied through slice<byte>(s): three conversions Go performs without a heap object, Atoi's 3 per run at go1.24.13. It reads 2 per run at go1.26.10 on windows and linux (identical test body). These string-conversion intermediates are removable by a converter change.
disclosures.history: want-zero AllocsPerRun assert: the closure's string([]byte) argument is proven non-escaping by Go's compiler and stays on the stack; the managed model must materialize an @string per run. The run's own unit note is COUNT, so golib's counter SAW these objects -- the COUNT arm of the 2026-09-05 ladder -- and the site family is one a named plan removes: string-conversion intermediates. Read at Atoi (src/core/strconv/atoi.cs:255-267): the test's string(bytes.Number) argument, the function-local `"Atoi"u8` constant materialised per call, and `range []byte(s)` copied through slice<byte>(s) -- three conversions Go performs without a heap object, which is Atoi's reading of 3. Only Atoi was decomposed; the other nine share the argument site. RE-READ AT go1.26.10 (2026-10-25, G): reading moved from 3 per run at go1.24.13 to 2 per run on windows and linux; the test body is identical at go1.24.13 and go1.26.10.
disclosures.reading: 2 per run on windows and linux -- go1.26.10 at d804094d7a (batch 37's tip), Release with tiering off; windows: 200 go2cs-runtime object allocations (8,000 bytes) over 100 runs, alloc-units-windows.tsv line 172 (claude/g-pass2-plan 966562828d); linux: 200 go2cs-runtime object allocations (8,000 bytes) over 100 runs, alloc-units-linux.tsv line 159 (claude/p1-alloc-reading 8d9d880ca2); both TSVs under docs/phase4/data/rebank-go1.26.10/; unit COUNT, a LOWER BOUND
disclosures.plan: RECORD: docs/phase4/DESIGN-string-byte-window.md §7 (the transient-conversion arm), stages 2 and 3 (range []byte(s) is Atoi's and ParseUint's, strconv/atoi.cs:267 and :145), and docs/phase4/DESIGN-string-literal-allocation.md §8 arm C for the function-local const (fnAtoi). the string-conversion family -- an intermediate buffer Go never allocates for a conversion whose result is not retained: golib's builtin.tmpstring (the zero-copy transient @string the converter already emits for a map-READ key, docs/ConversionStrategies-Reference.md `m[string(b)]`) extended to a string(b) that the callee or comparison does not retain, with docs/phase4/DESIGN-string-byte-window.md as the converter-side recognition record. The family's other arms, read at Atoi: a function-local string constant hoisted by docs/phase4/DESIGN-string-literal-allocation.md §8 arm C, and `range []byte(s)` walked over the string's bytes without a copy, as Go's compiler does. Retires when a run reads 0 per run with the counter still charging the path; a reading at the want with the counter charging NOTHING is the byte arm (testing.AllocsPerRun's fallback) and would be a false retire. (Plan fixed up 2026-09-23 per COORD's ACCEPT-WITH-FIXES, ledger 3942e083ad.)
